context.note: note_* features describe the nearest note's body: the bounding box of its notehead, stem and flag, or of every notehead plus the stem and flag of its chord, without accidentals, dots or articulations; note_dx / note_dy are the symbol centre minus that box's centre, note_above / note_below mean the centre is above its top / below its bottom within 0.5 spaces of its sides, note_left / note_right left / right of its sides within 0.5 spaces of its top and bottom

input.name: input
input.layout: NCHW, one grey channel, black ink on white paper
input.resize: pad to square with paper, then bilinear resize

strokes.pen_width_note: fraction of the canvas; uniform width, round caps, no blur; 0.05 scored best on held-out writers, training covered 0.055-0.115
strokes.fraction: longer side of the strokes' bounding box as a fraction of the canvas: min(0.9, max(0.08, span / (3.0 * staff_space)))
strokes.staff_space: pixels between two staff lines in the strokes' coordinates
strokes.centre: bounding-box centre at the canvas centre, aspect preserved

head.note: the last layer, Linear(128 -> classes), with its trained weights. The `personal` Core ML function / LiteRT signature takes a copy as inputs head_w (classes x 128) and head_b (classes) and gives back the features that layer reads, so an app can train the layer on the device from its users' replies; fed these weights it computes exactly what the default function does
